clue.text: Marine creature, small, this far out

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of this far are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea creature that is small and located a long way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the picture of distance, but it is what tells you to shuffle 'this far'.
explanation.definitionFit: This five-armed echinoderm lives on the sea floor, so it is a sea-dwelling animal.

clue.text: Tell Independent politician to get skill

parts.note: I is a common abbreviation for Independent, as in election results
MP, Member of Parliament, is the crossword's usual politician
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Telling an independent MP to acquire some ability.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on or communicate it to someone.

clue.text: Messy location limiting a period in hotel

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so the letter a sits inside the messy location

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is the proverbial messy place

explanation.surface: A grubby hotel room cuts short someone's time there.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit spent at a hotel is called a stay, a span of residence away from home.

clue.text: Soil surrounding grain farmed initially with contempt

indicators.note: surrounding means the soil synonym wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to soil something is to sully or dirty it
corn is a general word for grain

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of farmed

explanation.surface: Earth piled round a crop that was farmed, all done with disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts CORNF inside SULLY, splitting it after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting scornfully means acting with disdain, so it is a synonym for doing it with contempt.

clue.text: Pitman going round wrong purveyor of headgear

indicators.note: going round means the pitman word encloses the other piece

parts.note: a pitman is a man who works down a mine pit, a miner
ill can mean wrong or bad, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: A coal miner turning bad and becoming a hat seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and sells hats, especially women's hats, so supplies headgear.

clue.text: Judge old bottle capable of providing cheer

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A judge's old bottle of drink that can still cheer one up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jovial person is jolly and good-humoured, the sort to spread merriment.

clue.text: Edited topical item — Saving Energy — led by car offering computer control?

indicators.note: led by means the car word goes in front

parts.note: auto is a short word for a car, an automobile

indicators.note: edited means reworked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
saving here means except, so the energy letter is left out

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about energy saving and cars, revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as conserving energy, but it means 'except', so the E is removed before 'Edited' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot steers an aircraft or vehicle by computer, hence the query on the definition.

clue.text: Collector and historian describing tanks containing moulded tin

indicators.note: containing means the tanks word holds the rearranged tin inside it

parts.note: aquarian is the adjective for aquariums, the tanks fish live in

indicators.note: moulded means shaped anew, so the letters of tin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collector writes about fish tanks that hold some cast metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing tanks' is a single adjective, the word for things to do with aquariums, and 'containing' puts the rearranged tin inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiquarian studies or collects relics of the past, so is both collector and student of history.

clue.text: Looking unhappy about navy at the third level

indicators.note: about means the unhappy word goes round the navy abbreviation

parts.note: teary means tearful, looking unhappy
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Someone tearful over the state of the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ternary means threefold or of the third order, so it fits a third rank.

clue.text: English explorer not entirely fair about booze

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the drink
not entirely means the fair synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: fair and right both mean just
ale is beer, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: An English adventurer is a bit unfair where drinking is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' here means just or proper, not light-coloured or pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was the Elizabethan courtier who sailed to the Americas.

clue.text: Awkward youngster guided to follow books found in garden and on ship

indicators.note: found in means these pieces sit inside the garden word

parts.note: to hoe is to work a garden with a tool

indicators.note: to follow means the guided word comes after the books

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book, so BB is books
led means guided
a hoy is an old small coasting vessel

explanation.surface: A clumsy teenager follows instructions in the garden and aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here, to work the soil with a hoe, and the books and guided pieces split that tool word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbledehoy is an old word for a clumsy, gawky adolescent boy.

clue.text: Extinction? Mostly ask questions of the French and America

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to quiz someone is to ask them questions
et is the French word for and
US is America

explanation.surface: Asking about something dying out, of the French and of America.
explanation.definitionFit: A quietus is release from life, death, an end, so loosely an extinction.

clue.text: Collapse in membership fees? I study sources of club expenditure

parts.note: subs are subscriptions paid by members
a den is a private room for study

indicators.note: sources of means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A fall in club subscriptions, studied by looking at what the club spends.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidence is ground sinking or caving in, a collapse.

clue.text: Cooler to attack supporters?

parts.note: a fan cools things down
to club is to strike or attack

explanation.surface: Does a cooling device go on the offensive?
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised group of admirers of a performer or team.

clue.text: Remains in party after leader goes

indicators.note: after leader goes means the party word loses its first letter

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: Someone stays in the party once its leader departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is what is left after burning, such as cremated human remains.

clue.text: Duke leading crowd right to the end? He has no serious intent

indicators.note: leading means the duke letter goes in front
to the end means the letter for right moves from the front of the crowd word to its back

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A duke heading a mob, with the right wing pushed to the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the end' moves the right letter from the front of the crowd word to its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler is a dilettante who takes up activities casually rather than earnestly.

clue.text: A shade hard, ultimately? Certainly difficult, we hear

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of hard

parts.note: yes means certainly

indicators.note: we hear means the word for difficult is sounded rather than spelt

parts.note: tough means difficult

explanation.surface: Is a colour hard at the last? Certainly tricky, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' applies only to TOUGH, giving TUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyestuff is a substance that gives colour, so it supplies a tint.

clue.text: Pass on, leaving item of punctuation

indicators.note: leaving means the word on goes out of the punctuation mark

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark

explanation.surface: Pass on something but keep a comma or full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a mountain pass, the low point of a ridge between peaks.

clue.text: Champion sweet I distributed — most like toffee

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for champion, as at dog shows

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of sweet I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A champion hands out sweets, the chewiest toffees.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is famously sticky and needs much chomping, so the superlative fits.

clue.text: Fellow from Fair Isle, possibly — or fellow from Middle East

indicators.note: possibly means the remaining letters might be arranged another way
from means taken away from, so the fellow letter is removed

explanation.surface: A man from Fair Isle, or from the Middle East. Fair Isle is a Shetland island famed for knitwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes F, leaving AIRISLE for 'possibly' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Scrum getting our side in uproar

parts.note: a ruck is a loose rugby scrum
us means our side, the speakers' team

explanation.surface: A rugby scrum puts our team in a state of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruckus is a noisy commotion or disturbance.

clue.text: Vote in favour to split period of financial reporting?

parts.note: yea is a vote for, as opposed to nay
to rend is to tear apart or split

explanation.surface: Voting yes to divide up the accounting period.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies close their accounts at the end of the annual cycle, when results are reported.

clue.text: Get agitated time after time in A&E

indicators.note: in means the time pieces sit between A and E

parts.note: A and E are the letters printed either side of the ampersand

indicators.note: after means the T comes behind the era

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Worked up after waiting hours on end in the hospital's A&E department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is to stir air into a liquid, agitating it.

clue.text: Knight, embraced by niece, getting disordered item of apparel

indicators.note: embraced by means the knight letters are held inside the other piece
disordered means the letters of niece are jumbled

explanation.surface: A knight hugged by his niece ends up with rumpled clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is KT here, not the chess N; 'disordered' acts on niece alone, and 'embraced by' sets the knight letters inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a tie worn round the collar, a garment accessory.

clue.text: Hide error in repair?

parts.note: an animal's fur is its hide or pelt
bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: Covering up a blunder made in a repair.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To furbish is to polish up or renovate, restoring something.

clue.text: Lose it, following cheeky comments

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lip is impudent talk

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper after hearing insolent remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is to go into a sudden rage, an idiom for losing control.

clue.text: "Fact is, if you set out … well, there's nothing to add"

indicators.note: set out signals scattering, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker states the facts and then declares the subject closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' belongs to the fodder; only 'out' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a point so obvious that no further explanation is needed.
